page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical Intel cores via simultaneous multithreading, paired with 16 GB of system memory. Built on x86_64 architecture, its processor incorporates modern execution features, including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). It does not include integrated GPUs or onboard local storage, necessitating reliance on network-attached block storage for persistent data. Dedicated IPv4 addresses are also not bundled with the instance by default.

Benchmark results demonstrate balanced single-threaded execution alongside constrained multi-threaded capacity consistent with its 4-vCPU footprint. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1,807.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,561.99, placing it squarely in the middle 50% tier of cloud instances. However, due to its low physical core count, parallel throughput metrics fall into the bottom 25% bracket, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,100.0, a PassMark CPU score of 6,010.98, and a Clang software compilation score of 4,500.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 32.36 GB/sec read and 21.01 GB/sec write on uncached 256 MB blocks.

Network-facing throughput metrics present steady mid-tier capability, showing static web serving throughput of 6.53 GB/sec and average single-thread compression speeds. Micro-benchmarks for database operations and Redis SET operations (4.62 million operations/sec) land in the lower quartile, reflecting the limits of a 4-vCPU general-purpose footprint without local NVMe scratch storage. Small LLM text generation reaches 118.57 tokens/sec on a 135M model, but prompt ingestion drops to lower percentiles when scaling to 7B models.

From an engineering perspective, the n4-standard-4 provides cost-efficient baseline compute for workloads that require modest hardware density without overprovisioning cores. With a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, it is best suited for lightweight web serving, application middleware, API microservices, staging environments, and intermediate text processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 4 vCPUs (2 physical Intel x86_64 cores with hyperthreading) and 16 GB of memory. The platform features modern vector and matrix instructions, including AVX-512 and AMX, but does not bundle local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance shows mid-tier single-core CPU throughput (Geekbench single-core 1,807.0; stress-ng single-core 1,561.99) and average web serving bandwidth of 6.53 GB/sec. Its multi-threaded processing and memory bandwidth are limited by the small core footprint, placing metrics such as the PassMark CPU score (6,010.98) and multi-core Geekbench score (4,100.0) in the lower quartile. The n4-standard-4 is suited for web serving, microservices, lightweight application backends, and moderate utility compute jobs.
